blocks.text: Through Indigenous ecological knowledge, collective memory and personal testimony, Museu da Pessoa invites a fundamental reconsideration of humanity’s relationship with the living world.

Curated by Indigenous Brazilian thinker, writer and environmental activist Ailton Krenak and Museu da Pessoa founder Karen Worcman, Have You Ever Listened to the Earth? challenges the anthropocentric thinking that has historically separated humanity from nature.

Drawing on the museum’s archive of more than 20,000 life stories, the exhibition foregrounds the experiences and inherited knowledge of communities across Brazil’s six biomes. Through oral histories, audiovisual narratives and immersive installations, it explores the connections between territory, cultural memory and ecological interdependence.

At its centre is a monumental textile installation collectively produced from discarded materials gathered across Brazil. Visitors are invited to contribute their own stories, becoming active participants in an evolving archive. Rather than positioning humanity as nature’s custodian, the exhibition proposes listening as a way to recognise our place within a broader ecology of living and non-living beings. museudapessoa.org+1
On exhibition from 4 December 2026. Museu da Pessoa, Rio de Janeiro.
